distance_model.basis: WGS84 great-circle distance between authored reconstruction points multiplied by a mode-specific path sinuosity factor
distance_model.historical_scope: Calibration is a gameplay editorial proposal, not a measured 1230 travel record. The map is an authored reconstruction and the modern delta is only a broad framework.

walking_field_study.summary: Table 2 reports observed walking speeds around 1.39 m/s on a trail and 1.2 m/s in forest.
walking_field_study.use: Modern comparison point for trail and forest rates only; not a medieval or local measurement.

paddled_boat_experiment.quote: The speed while paddling under normal conditions reached up to 5.5km/hour.
paddled_boat_experiment.use: Experimental upper comparison point for a paddled craft; craft, water, and conditions differ from the lower Dvina.

lower_dvina_estuary_current.quote: The current velocities were about 21–22 cm/s at mainstream station 1; the current velocity increased to 45 cm/s at station 2.
lower_dvina_estuary_current.scope: Leshchev et al. 2015 reports SEAGUARD RCM measurements at six estuary stations on 17–28 March 2014 in winter low runoff; tidal slowing and a brief reversal were observed. These modern station readings do not establish a uniform local 1230 current. They only bound a plausible magnitude.

delta_framework.quote: Вершина дельты находится вблизи центра г. Архангельска, откуда веерообразно расходятся основные рукава
delta_framework.use: Supports the broad modern branching frame only; does not establish 1230 channels, local travel speeds, or current velocity.

current.direction: positive downstream toward the White Sea; negative upstream
current.rationale: The 1.0 km/h bias is an editorial value within the magnitude of cited modern winter estuary observations (about 0.76–1.62 km/h for 0.21–0.45 m/s), not an adopted station measurement. It is provisional and must be replaced or affirmed during review; still-water body-type overrides take precedence.
current.water_body_override_rationale: Candidate water-body type controls the local current bias: still-water old channels and reed backwaters use 0 km/h. Resolve from the assigned water body, not from a nearby river skeleton or line name.

path.rationale: Moderate walking pace below the cited modern trail study; factor allows a winding path.

shore.rationale: Walking on a variable bank or landing edge, slower and less direct than a clear path.

boat_downstream.rationale: Moderate paddled-craft speed below the cited experimental maximum, with the provisional current added to speed over ground.

boat_upstream.rationale: Same still-water craft speed as downstream; provisional current is subtracted from speed over ground.

boat_across.rationale: Reduced cross-channel progress under an uncertain angle to the flow; current magnitude is not added along this path.

boat_open_water.rationale: Open-water craft rate without channel-current adjustment; a small factor allows a non-straight crossing.

forest_track.rationale: Editorial walking pace within the reviewer-specified 2.5–3.0 km/h range for forest tracks; factor 1.3 allows a moderately winding track. Modern field-study rates are comparison points only.

wetland_path.rationale: Editorial pace for a marked wetland path, following the reviewer-specified approximate 1.5 km/h; factor 1.3 allows a moderately winding path. No local historical measurement is claimed.

offroad.rationale: Editorial direct-crossing pace and factor 1.0 for movement described as straight across country; speed and factor are provisional, not measured.

boat_still_water.rationale: Uses the approved still-water craft speed and route factor for a boat moving in a typed still-water body; no current is added or subtracted.

editorial_policy.rounding: nearest whole minute, ties follow JavaScript Math.round; minimum one minute for positive distances
editorial_policy.legacy_minutes: Retained as old-to-proposed comparison only; they do not calibrate the proposed duration.

route_trace_residual_factor.rationale: Residual adjustment for unmeasured bends and access within an authored route trace; the trace already captures its drawn length, so full mode sinuosity would count bends twice.

editorial_policy.suggested_segment_count: ceil(proposed_minutes / 30), minimum 1; informational only and does not split the graph
editorial_policy.open_water_classification: line_kind=open_water selects boat_open_water even when the route is water-bound; current-relative direction remains reported separately but does not affect speed
editorial_policy.unknown_method: No proposed minutes are emitted when movement mode cannot be classified from line-name candidate / route method.
editorial_policy.water_body_current_precedence: Resolve current from the candidate water body assigned to the line. A matching current.water_body_type_overrides_kmh entry overrides the global current value; a zero-current water body uses boat_still_water for boat movement and reports no river direction.
